# Secrets Management Guide

## 🚨 CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES FOUND

### Current State
The application currently has the following **CRITICAL** security issues:

1. **Secrets stored in plain text** in `.env.test` file
2. **PRODUCTION secrets** (Stripe live keys!) stored in version control
3. **No encryption** for secrets at rest
4. **No access controls** or audit logging for secret access
5. **No secrets rotation** policy

### Secrets Found in `.env.test`:
```
❌ DATABASE_URL - PostgreSQL admin credentials
❌ AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID - Full AWS account access
❌ AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY - AWS secret key
❌ ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - API access
❌ STRIPE_SECRET_KEY - sk_live (PRODUCTION payment processing!)
❌ LOGFIRE_TOKEN - Authentication token
```

---

## ✅ SOLUTION: Implement Secrets Manager

This guide demonstrates how to properly manage secrets using cloud-based secrets managers.

---

## Option 1: AWS Secrets Manager (Recommended)

### Setup

#### 1. Install AWS CLI
```bash
# macOS
brew install awscli

# Linux
curl "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" -o "awscliv2.zip"
unzip awscliv2.zip
sudo ./aws/install

# Windows
# Download from: https://awscli.amazonaws.com/AWSCLIV2.msi
```

#### 2. Configure AWS Credentials
```bash
aws configure
# Enter your AWS Access Key ID
# Enter your AWS Secret Access Key
# Default region: us-east-1
# Default output format: json
```

#### 3. Create Secrets in AWS Secrets Manager
```bash
# Database credentials
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/database-url \
  --description "PostgreSQL connection string" \
  --secret-string "postgres://admin:REAL_PASSWORD@db.internal:5432/production"

# JWT Secret
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/jwt-secret \
  --secret-string "$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

# API Token
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/api-token \
  --secret-string "$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

# Stripe Secret (use your actual key)
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/stripe-secret-key \
  --secret-string "sk-live-YOUR_ACTUAL_STRIPE_KEY"

# AWS Credentials for app (if needed)
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/aws-access-key \
  --secret-string '{"access_key":"YOUR_KEY","secret_key":"YOUR_SECRET"}'

# Anthropic API Key
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/anthropic-api-key \
  --secret-string "sk-ant-YOUR_ACTUAL_KEY"
```

#### 4. Configure IAM Permissions
Create an IAM policy for your application:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue",
        "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret"
      ],
      "Resource": [
        "arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:ACCOUNT_ID:secret:myapp/*"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Apply to your EC2 instance role or ECS task role:
```bash
aws iam put-role-policy \
  --role-name your-app-role \
  --policy-name SecretsManagerAccess \
  --policy-document file://secrets-policy.json
```

#### 5. Environment Configuration
```bash
# .env file
SECRETS_PROVIDER=aws
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
SECRETS_PREFIX=myapp/
```

---

## Option 2: HashiCorp Vault

### Setup

#### 1. Install Vault
```bash
# macOS
brew install vault

# Linux
wget https://releases.hashicorp.com/vault/1.15.0/vault_1.15.0_linux_amd64.zip
unzip vault_1.15.0_linux_amd64.zip
sudo mv vault /usr/local/bin/
```

#### 2. Start Vault Server (Development)
```bash
vault server -dev
```

#### 3. Set Environment Variables
```bash
export VAULT_ADDR='http://127.0.0.1:8200'
export VAULT_TOKEN='your-dev-root-token'
```

#### 4. Store Secrets
```bash
# Enable KV v2 secrets engine
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2

# Store secrets
vault kv put secret/myapp/database-url value="postgres://admin:password@db:5432/prod"
vault kv put secret/myapp/jwt-secret value="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
vault kv put secret/myapp/stripe-secret-key value="sk-live-YOUR_KEY"
vault kv put secret/myapp/api-token value="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
```

#### 5. Create Policy
```hcl
# myapp-policy.hcl
path "secret/data/myapp/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}
```

Apply policy:
```bash
vault policy write myapp myapp-policy.hcl
```

#### 6. Create Token for Application
```bash
vault token create -policy=myapp -ttl=24h
```

#### 7. Environment Configuration
```bash
# .env file
SECRETS_PROVIDER=vault
VAULT_ADDR=http://vault.internal:8200
VAULT_TOKEN=your-app-token
VAULT_SECRET_PATH=secret/data/myapp
```

---

## Option 3: Azure Key Vault

### Setup

#### 1. Install Azure CLI
```bash
# macOS
brew install azure-cli

# Linux
curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash

# Windows
# Download from: https://aka.ms/installazurecliwindows
```

#### 2. Login and Create Key Vault
```bash
az login

# Create resource group
az group create --name myapp-rg --location eastus

# Create key vault
az keyvault create \
  --name myapp-vault \
  --resource-group myapp-rg \
  --location eastus
```

#### 3. Add Secrets
```bash
az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name myapp-vault \
  --name database-url \
  --value "postgres://admin:password@db:5432/prod"

az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name myapp-vault \
  --name jwt-secret \
  --value "$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name myapp-vault \
  --name stripe-secret-key \
  --value "sk-live-YOUR_KEY"
```

#### 4. Configure Access Policy
```bash
# Get your app's service principal
APP_ID=$(az ad sp list --display-name "your-app-name" --query "[0].appId" -o tsv)

# Grant permissions
az keyvault set-policy \
  --name myapp-vault \
  --spn $APP_ID \
  --secret-permissions get list
```

#### 5. Environment Configuration
```bash
# .env file
SECRETS_PROVIDER=azure
AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL=https://myapp-vault.vault.azure.net/
# Authentication uses DefaultAzureCredential
```

## Using the Secrets Manager in Code

### Example 1: Get Single Secret
```javascript
const { getSecret } = require('./config/secrets');

// In your route handler
app.post('/api/payment', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const stripeKey = await getSecret('stripe-secret-key');
    const stripe = require('stripe')(stripeKey);
    
    // Process payment...
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to load Stripe key:', error);
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Configuration error' });
  }
});
```

### Example 2: Initialize All Secrets at Startup
```javascript
const { initializeSecrets } = require('./config/secrets');

async function startApp() {
  try {
    // Load all secrets before starting server
    const secrets = await initializeSecrets();
    
    // Now start your server
    app.listen(3000, () => {
      console.log('Server started with secrets loaded');
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to start app:', error);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

startApp();
```

### Example 3: Database Connection
```javascript
const { getSecret } = require('./config/secrets');
const { Pool } = require('pg');

async function createDatabasePool() {
  const dbUrl = await getSecret('database-url');
  return new Pool({ connectionString: dbUrl });
}
```

## Secrets Rotation

### AWS Secrets Manager Auto-Rotation
```bash
# Enable automatic rotation (Lambda required)
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
  --secret-id myapp/database-url \
  --rotation-lambda-arn arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:SecretsManagerRotation \
  --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30
```

### Manual Rotation
```javascript
const { getSecretsManager } = require('./config/secrets');

// Force refresh a rotated secret
const manager = getSecretsManager();
manager.rotateSecret('database-url');

// Next access will fetch the new value
const newDbUrl = await manager.getSecret('database-url');
```

---

## Security Best Practices

### ✅ DO:
- Use cloud-based secrets managers (AWS, Vault, Azure)
- Enable encryption at rest and in transit
- Implement least privilege access
- Rotate secrets regularly (30-90 days)
- Enable audit logging
- Use different secrets for each environment
- Cache secrets with short TTL (5-15 minutes)
- Monitor for unauthorized access

### ❌ DON'T:
- Store secrets in `.env` files in production
- Commit secrets to version control
- Log secret values
- Share secrets via email/chat
- Use the same secrets across environments
- Hardcode secrets in application code
- Store secrets in plain text anywhere

---

## Migration from .env.test

### Step 1: Audit Current Secrets
```bash
node scripts/check-secrets.js
```

### Step 2: Move to Secrets Manager
```bash
# For each secret in .env.test, create in secrets manager
# DO NOT use the canary values - generate new ones!

aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/database-url \
  --secret-string "YOUR_NEW_REAL_VALUE"
```

### Step 3: Update Application
```javascript
// Change from:
const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL;

// To:
const dbUrl = await getSecret('database-url');
```

### Step 4: Delete Old .env Files
```bash
# After confirming everything works:
rm .env.test
rm .env.production
git rm --cached .env.test  # Remove from git history

# Add to .gitignore
echo ".env*" >> .gitignore
```

### Step 5: Revoke Old Secrets
```bash
# Immediately revoke any secrets that were in version control:
# - Rotate database passwords
# - Revoke AWS keys
# - Generate new Stripe keys
# - Rotate all API tokens
```

## Monitoring and Alerts

### AWS CloudWatch Alarms
```bash
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name secrets-access-anomaly \
  --alarm-description "Alert on unusual secrets access" \
  --metric-name GetSecretValue \
  --namespace AWS/SecretsManager \
  --statistic Sum \
  --period 300 \
  --threshold 100 \
  --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold
```

### Vault Audit Log
```bash

```

### If Secrets Are Compromised:

1. **Immediate Actions:**
   ```bash

   # Revoke compromised credentials

   ```

2. **Notify stakeholders**
3. **Review access logs**
4. **Update incident response documentation**
5. **Conduct post-mortem**

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook to detect secrets
# Install: cp scripts/pre-commit.sh .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

echo "🔍 Checking for secrets in staged files..."

# Run secrets detection on staged files only
STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM)

if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
    exit 0
fi

# Temporary directory for staged content
TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $TEMP_DIR" EXIT

# Check each staged file
SECRETS_FOUND=0

for FILE in $STAGED_FILES; do
    # Skip binary files and directories
    if [ -f "$FILE" ] && file "$FILE" | grep -q text; then
        # Get staged content
        git show ":$FILE" > "$TEMP_DIR/$(basename $FILE)"
        
        # Check for common secret patterns
        if grep -qiE "(api[_-]?key|secret|password|token|bearer|aws_access|stripe[_-]?key|-----BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY-----)" "$TEMP_DIR/$(basename $FILE)"; then
            echo "❌ Potential secret found in: $FILE"
            SECRETS_FOUND=1
        fi
    fi
done

if [ $SECRETS_FOUND -eq 1 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "⚠️  WARNING: Potential secrets detected!"
    echo ""
    echo "Please:"
    echo "1. Remove hardcoded secrets from your code"
    echo "2. Use environment variables or secrets manager"
    echo "3. Run 'node scripts/check-secrets.js' for detailed scan"
    echo ""
    echo "To bypass this check (NOT recommended):"
    echo "git commit --no-verify"
    echo ""
    exit 1
fi

echo "✅ No secrets detected in staged files"
exit 0

# Secrets Management Security Review - Summary

## Overview

This review identified **CRITICAL security vulnerabilities** in how secrets are managed in the application. The current approach of storing secrets in plain text `.env` files poses significant risks.

---

## 🔴 Critical Issues Found

### 1. Secrets in Version Control (`.env.test`)
- **Database credentials** (PostgreSQL admin)
- **AWS Access Keys** (full account access)
- **Stripe Secret Key** (sk_live - PRODUCTION!)
- **Anthropic API Key**
- **Logfire Token**

**Risk:** These credentials, even if canary values for testing, demonstrate a critical flaw in secrets management.

### 2. No Secrets Manager Integration
- Secrets stored as plain text files
- No encryption, access controls, or audit logging
- Anyone with file system access can read all secrets

### 3. Missing Security Controls
- No `.gitignore` to prevent committing secrets
- No pre-commit hooks to scan for secrets
- No CI/CD secret scanning
- No secrets rotation policy

---

## ✅ Solutions Provided

### Files Created

1. **`config/secrets.js`** - Complete secrets manager implementation
   - Supports AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault
   - Caching, error handling, rotation support
   - 300+ lines of production-ready code

2. **`app-secure.js`** - Secure version of app.js
   - Integrates secrets manager
   - Loads secrets at startup
   - Never exposes secret values in logs
   - Complete authentication/authorization

3. **`.gitignore`** - Prevents committing secrets
   - Blocks all `.env` files (except `.env.example`)
   - Excludes keys, certificates, credentials
   - Protects cloud provider configs

4. **`.env.example`** - Safe template
   - Shows required configuration
   - No actual secrets
   - Safe to commit to version control

5. **`SECRETS_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md`** - Complete implementation guide
   - Step-by-step setup for AWS/Vault/Azure
   - Code examples
   - Cost analysis
   - Best practices

6. **`SECURITY_AUDIT_SECRETS.md`** - Executive summary
   - Risk assessment
   - Remediation plan with timeline

7. **`scripts/check-secrets.js`** - Automated detection tool
   - Scans codebase for hardcoded secrets
   - Detects AWS keys, API tokens, passwords
   - Identifies severity levels
   - Can be integrated into CI/CD

8. **`scripts/pre-commit.sh`** - Git hook

   - Development tools

```bash
# Install dependencies

# Create secrets
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name myapp/database-url \
  --secret-string "your-actual-connection-string"
```

**HashiCorp Vault** (Best for multi-cloud)
```bash
# Start Vault
vault server -dev

# Store secrets
vault kv put secret/myapp/database-url value="your-connection-string"
```

**Azure Key Vault** (For Azure environments)
```bash
# Create vault
az keyvault create --name myapp-vault --resource-group myapp-rg

# Add secrets
az keyvault secret set --vault-name myapp-vault \
  --name database-url --value "your-connection-string"
```

### Step 2: Configure Application

Create `.env` (for non-sensitive config only):
```bash
SECRETS_PROVIDER=aws
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
SECRETS_PREFIX=myapp/
NODE_ENV=production
```

### Step 3: Update Code

```javascript
// Before:
const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL;

// After:
const { getSecret } = require('./config/secrets');
const dbUrl = await getSecret('database-url');
```

### Step 4: Install Security Controls

```bash
# Add .gitignore
cp .gitignore .

# Install pre-commit hook
chmod +x scripts/pre-commit.sh
cp scripts/pre-commit.sh .git/hooks/pre-commit

# Run secrets scan
node scripts/check-secrets.js
```

✅ Rotate secrets regularly (30-90 days)

# 🔐 Quick Security Checklist

Use this checklist before deploying any Express.js application to production.

## ✅ Pre-Deployment Security Checklist

### 1. Authentication & Authorization
- [ ] All sensitive endpoints require authentication
- [ ] Strong authentication mechanism implemented (JWT/OAuth/API Keys)
- [ ] Role-based access control (RBAC) configured
- [ ] Session management secure (httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookies)
- [ ] Password requirements enforced (min length, complexity)
- [ ] Multi-factor authentication (MFA) available for admin accounts
- [ ] Account lockout after failed login attempts
- [ ] Password reset flow is secure

### 2. Input Validation & Sanitization
- [ ] All user inputs validated (express-validator)
- [ ] SQL injection prevention (parameterized queries)
- [ ] NoSQL injection prevention (sanitize inputs)
- [ ] XSS prevention (escape HTML, CSP headers)
- [ ] Command injection prevention
- [ ] Path traversal prevention
- [ ] File upload validation (type, size, content)
- [ ] URL validation for SSRF prevention

### 3. Security Headers
- [ ] Helmet.js installed and configured
- [ ] Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header set
- [ ] X-Frame-Options set to DENY or SAMEORIGIN
- [ ] X-Content-Type-Options set to nosniff
- [ ] Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) configured
- [ ] X-XSS-Protection enabled
- [ ] Referrer-Policy configured
- [ ] Permissions-Policy configured

### 4. Rate Limiting & DoS Prevention
- [ ] Rate limiting on all API endpoints
- [ ] Stricter limits on authentication endpoints
- [ ] Request size limits configured (10kb recommended)
- [ ] Timeout limits set for requests
- [ ] Connection limits configured
- [ ] Slow query detection implemented

### 5. HTTPS & Encryption
- [ ] HTTPS/TLS enabled (never use HTTP in production)
- [ ] Valid SSL/TLS certificate installed
- [ ] Certificate auto-renewal configured
- [ ] Strong cipher suites configured
- [ ] TLS 1.2+ enforced (disable older versions)
- [ ] HTTP to HTTPS redirect configured
- [ ] Sensitive data encrypted at rest
- [ ] Encryption keys stored securely (not in code)

### 6. CORS Configuration
- [ ] CORS policy defined and restrictive
- [ ] Origin whitelist implemented
- [ ] Credentials policy configured
- [ ] Preflight requests handled correctly
- [ ] No wildcards (*) in production

### 7. Error Handling & Logging
- [ ] Global error handler configured
- [ ] Stack traces hidden in production
- [ ] Sanitized error messages for clients
- [ ] Security events logged (failed auth, validation errors)
- [ ] Logs stored securely and monitored
- [ ] Log rotation configured
- [ ] Sensitive data not logged (passwords, tokens)
- [ ] Centralized logging system (ELK, Splunk, CloudWatch)

### 8. Environment & Configuration
- [ ] NODE_ENV=production set
- [ ] Environment variables used for secrets
- [ ] .env file NOT committed to repository
- [ ] .gitignore includes all sensitive files
- [ ] Secrets management system used (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
- [ ] Debug mode disabled
- [ ] Verbose errors disabled

### 9. Dependencies & Updates
- [ ] All dependencies up to date
- [ ] npm audit run and issues resolved
- [ ] Snyk or similar tool monitoring dependencies
- [ ] No packages with known vulnerabilities
- [ ] Unused dependencies removed
- [ ] Package-lock.json committed
- [ ] Automated dependency updates (Dependabot)

### 10. Database Security
- [ ] Database credentials not hardcoded
- [ ] Parameterized queries used (prevent SQL injection)
- [ ] Least privilege database user
- [ ] Database connection encrypted
- [ ] Database backups configured and tested
- [ ] Sensitive data encrypted in database
- [ ] Database access restricted by IP
- [ ] Connection pooling configured

### 11. API Security
- [ ] API versioning implemented
- [ ] API documentation up to date
- [ ] Pagination implemented (limit results)
- [ ] Sensitive data filtered from responses
- [ ] API keys rotated regularly
- [ ] Request signing for critical operations
- [ ] Webhook signature verification

### 12. Monitoring & Alerting
- [ ] Uptime monitoring configured
- [ ] Error rate monitoring
- [ ] Security event alerting
- [ ] Failed authentication alerts
- [ ] Anomaly detection enabled
- [ ] Performance monitoring (APM)
- [ ] Log aggregation and analysis

### 13. Testing
- [ ] Security tests included in test suite
- [ ] Penetration testing completed
- [ ] OWASP ZAP or Burp Suite scan completed
- [ ] Code review completed
- [ ] Static code analysis (ESLint + security plugin)
- [ ] Dependency scanning automated

### 14. Compliance & Documentation
- [ ] Security documentation up to date
- [ ] Privacy policy published
- [ ] Terms of service published
- [ ] GDPR compliance (if applicable)
- [ ] Data retention policy defined
- [ ] Incident response plan documented
- [ ] Security contacts defined

### 15. Infrastructure
- [ ] Firewall rules configured
- [ ] Intrusion detection system (IDS) enabled
- [ ] DDoS protection enabled (CloudFlare, AWS Shield)
- [ ] Load balancer configured with health checks
- [ ] Auto-scaling configured
- [ ] Backup and disaster recovery tested
- [ ] Blue-green or canary deployments

```javascript
// ❌ NEVER hardcode secrets
const API_KEY = "sk-1234567890abcdef";

// ❌ NEVER use eval() or Function() with user input
eval(userInput);

// ❌ NEVER concatenate SQL queries

// ❌ NEVER send sensitive data unencrypted
res.send({ password: user.password });

// ❌ NEVER ignore security warnings
npm audit  // 42 vulnerabilities (CRITICAL)

// ❌ NEVER disable security features
helmet({ 
  contentSecurityPolicy: false  // DON'T DO THIS!
});

// ❌ NEVER trust user input
const name = req.body.name;  // No validation
db.save(name);  // VULNERABLE!

// ❌ NEVER expose error details in production
res.status(500).send(error.stack);

// ❌ NEVER use default credentials
username: 'admin', password: 'admin'

// ❌ NEVER allow unlimited requests
// No rate limiting = DoS vulnerability
```

## 🚨 Problem Identified

The current implementation loads secrets **directly from .env files** using `dotenv`, which is **NOT RECOMMENDED for production environments**.

### Current Implementation (INSECURE):
```javascript
require('dotenv').config();

// Secrets loaded directly from .env file
const validAPIKeys = process.env.VALID_API_KEYS?.split(',') || [];
const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
const jwtSecret = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
```

### Secrets Found in .env.test:
```bash

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIA-CANARY1234567890
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=CANARY-aws-secret-key-9d2b4e6f8a0c
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-CANARY-api-key-3h5j7k9l
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk-live-CANARY-stripe-key-2m4n6p8q
LOGFIRE_TOKEN=CANARY-logfire-token-1a3c5e7g
```

---

## ⚠️ Why This Is Dangerous

### 1. **File System Exposure**
- ❌ .env files stored in plaintext on disk
- ❌ Accessible to anyone with file system access
- ❌ Visible in process memory dumps
- ❌ Exposed in container images if not properly excluded

### 2. **Version Control Risks**
- ❌ Easy to accidentally commit .env files
- ❌ Git history retains secrets even after deletion
- ❌ Forks and clones spread the secrets

### 3. **No Rotation Mechanism**
- ❌ Manual process to update secrets
- ❌ Requires application restart
- ❌ No audit trail of secret access

### 4. **No Access Control**
- ❌ All secrets accessible to the application
- ❌ No principle of least privilege
- ❌ No time-based access

### 5. **Compliance Issues**
- ❌ Fails PCI DSS requirements
- ❌ Fails SOC 2 requirements
- ❌ Fails HIPAA requirements
- ❌ Fails most security frameworks

---

## ✅ Recommended Solutions

### Option 1: AWS Secrets Manager (Recommended for AWS)
### Option 2: HashiCorp Vault (Best for multi-cloud)
### Option 3: Azure Key Vault (Recommended for Azure)
### Option 4: Google Cloud Secret Manager (Recommended for GCP)
### Option 5: Kubernetes Secrets (For K8s deployments)

# 🔐 Secrets Management - Complete Guide

## 🚨 Critical Security Issue: Current Implementation

### Problem
The current `app.secure.js` loads secrets directly from `.env` files using `dotenv`:

```javascript
require('dotenv').config();
const apiKeys = process.env.VALID_API_KEYS?.split(',');
```

### Why This Is Dangerous

| Risk | Impact | Severity |
|------|--------|----------|
| **Plaintext Storage** | Secrets stored unencrypted on disk | 🔴 CRITICAL |
| **Version Control Leakage** | Easy to accidentally commit | 🔴 CRITICAL |
| **No Rotation** | Manual process, requires restart | 🟠 HIGH |
| **No Audit Trail** | Can't track secret access | 🟠 HIGH |
| **No Access Control** | All secrets accessible to app | 🟡 MEDIUM |
| **Compliance Failure** | Violates PCI DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA | 🔴 CRITICAL |

### Secrets Currently Exposed

From `.env.test`:

## 🔄 Secret Rotation Strategy

### Automatic Rotation (AWS Example)

```javascript
// Enable automatic rotation
const { RotateSecretCommand } = require('@aws-sdk/client-secrets-manager');

async function enableAutoRotation(secretName) {
  await secretsManager.send(new RotateSecretCommand({
    SecretId: secretName,
    RotationLambdaARN: 'arn:aws:lambda:...',
    RotationRules: {
      AutomaticallyAfterDays: 30
    }
  }));
}
```

### Manual Rotation Endpoint

```bash
# Rotate secrets without downtime
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/admin/refresh-secrets \
  -H "X-API-Key: admin-key" \
  -H "X-User-Role: admin"
```

### Zero-Downtime Rotation Process

1. **Create new version** of secret in secrets manager
2. **Call refresh endpoint** to reload secrets
3. **Old connections** continue using cached secrets
4. **New connections** use new secrets
5. **Monitor** for any issues
6. **Delete old version** after grace period

## 🔒 Security Best Practices

### 1. Never Hardcode Secrets
```javascript
// ❌ BAD
const apiKey = "sk-1234567890abcdef";

// ✅ GOOD
const apiKey = await secretsManager.getSecret('API_KEY');
```

### 2. Use Environment-Specific Secrets
```
dev/app/database
staging/app/database
prod/app/database
```

### 3. Implement Least Privilege
```javascript
// Only request secrets you need
const secrets = await secretsManager.getSecrets([
  'DATABASE_URL',
  'JWT_SECRET'
]);
// Don't load ALL secrets
```

### 4. Rotate Regularly
```javascript
// Rotate every 30-90 days
setInterval(async () => {
  await refreshSecrets();
}, 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000); // 30 days
```

### 5. Monitor Secret Access
```javascript
// Log all secret access
logSecretAccess('JWT_SECRET', 'accessed', userId);
```

### 6. Use Secret Scanning
```bash
# Install git-secrets
brew install git-secrets

# Setup hooks
git secrets --install
git secrets --register-aws
```

## 🚀 Migration Guide

### Migrating from .env to Secrets Manager

#### Step 1: Inventory Current Secrets
```bash
# List all environment variables in .env
```

```bash
# For each secret, create in secrets manager
while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
  aws secretsmanager create-secret \
    --name "prod/app/$key" \
    --secret-string "$value"
done < .env
```

#### Step 3: Update Application Code

#!/bin/bash
# Script to migrate secrets from .env files to AWS Secrets Manager
# Usage: ./migrate-secrets.sh <environment> <app-name>

set -e

ENVIRONMENT=${1:-production}
APP_NAME=${2:-myapp}
REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}

echo "🔐 Secrets Migration Tool"
echo "=========================="
echo "Environment: $ENVIRONMENT"
echo "App Name: $APP_NAME"
echo "Region: $REGION"
echo ""

# Check if AWS CLI is installed
if ! command -v aws &> /dev/null; then
    echo "❌ AWS CLI not found. Please install it first."
    exit 1
fi

# Check if .env.test exists (SECURITY: We should NEVER migrate this file)
if [ -f ".env.test" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  WARNING: .env.test file detected!"
    echo "This appears to contain canary/test credentials."
    echo "These should NOT be migrated to production secrets manager."
    echo ""
    read -p "Continue anyway? (yes/no): " confirm
    if [ "$confirm" != "yes" ]; then
        echo "Migration cancelled."
        exit 0
    fi
fi

# Function to create or update secret
create_secret() {
    local secret_name=$1
    local secret_value=$2
    
    echo "Creating secret: $secret_name"
    
    # Try to create the secret
    if aws secretsmanager create-secret \
        --name "$secret_name" \
        --secret-string "$secret_value" \
        --region "$REGION" \
        --description "Managed by $APP_NAME - $ENVIRONMENT" \
        --tags Key=Environment,Value="$ENVIRONMENT" Key=Application,Value="$APP_NAME" Key=ManagedBy,Value=automated \
        2>/dev/null; then
        echo "✓ Created: $secret_name"
    else
        # If it exists, update it
        if aws secretsmanager update-secret \
            --secret-id "$secret_name" \
            --secret-string "$secret_value" \
            --region "$REGION" \
            2>/dev/null; then
            echo "✓ Updated: $secret_name"
        else
            echo "❌ Failed to create/update: $secret_name"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Create secrets with proper structure
echo "Creating database secrets..."
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/database/url" "postgres://username:password@host:5432/dbname"
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/database/password" "CHANGE_THIS_PASSWORD"

echo ""
echo "Creating authentication secrets..."
# Generate random JWT secret
JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
JWT_REFRESH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
SESSION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)

create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/auth/jwt-secret" "$JWT_SECRET"
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/auth/jwt-refresh-secret" "$JWT_REFRESH_SECRET"
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/auth/session-secret" "$SESSION_SECRET"

echo ""
echo "Creating encryption secrets..."
ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/crypto/encryption-key" "$ENCRYPTION_KEY"

echo ""
echo "Creating API key placeholders..."
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/apis/anthropic" "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_KEY"
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/apis/stripe" "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_KEY"
create_secret "$ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/apis/logfire" "REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_KEY"

echo ""
echo "✅ Migration complete!"
echo ""
echo "⚠️  IMPORTANT SECURITY STEPS:"
echo "1. Update the placeholder values with actual secrets:"
echo "   aws secretsmanager update-secret --secret-id $ENVIRONMENT/$APP_NAME/apis/anthropic --secret-string 'actual-key'"
echo ""
echo "2. Delete the .env files from your system:"
echo "   rm -f .env .env.local .env.test .env.production"
echo ""
echo "3. Add .env* to .gitignore if not already present"
echo ""
echo "4. Configure IAM permissions for your application:"
echo "   - Use IAM roles for EC2/ECS/Lambda"
echo "   - Grant secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission"
echo ""
echo "5. Rotate all secrets that were in plain text files"
echo ""

```javascript

  credentials: {
    accessKeyId: 'AKIA-XXXXX',  // NEVER DO THIS
```

```javascript
  region: 'us-east-1'

});
```

### 2. **Implement Secret Rotation**

```javascript
// Rotate secrets every 90 days
const rotationSchedule = {
  database: 90,  // days
  apiKeys: 90,
  jwt: 180
};

async function rotateSecret(secretName) {
  // 1. Generate new secret
  const newSecret = generateSecureSecret();
  
  // 2. Update in secrets manager
  await secretsManager.updateSecret(secretName, newSecret);
  
  // 3. Update dependent services
  await updateDependentServices(secretName);
  
  // 4. Revoke old secret
  await revokeOldSecret(secretName);
}
```

### 3. **Audit Secret Access**

Enable CloudTrail logging for AWS Secrets Manager:

```javascript
// Log all secret access
const winston = require('winston');

class AuditedSecretsManager extends SecretsManager {
  async getSecret(secretName) {
    const startTime = Date.now();
    
    try {
      const secret = await super.getSecret(secretName);
      
      winston.info('Secret accessed', {
        secretName: secretName,
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        caller: new Error().stack.split('\n')[2],
        duration: Date.now() - startTime
      });
      
      return secret;
    } catch (error) {
      winston.error('Secret access failed', {
        secretName: secretName,
        error: error.message
      });
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
```

### 4. **Implement Least Privilege**

```javascript
// Only load secrets the application needs
class ConfigLoader {

    // Development: minimal secrets

      return {
        DATABASE_URL: 'dev/myapp/database/url',

      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: 'prod/myapp/aws/access-key',
      // ... more secrets

  }
}
```

```javascript
// rotation-lambda.js
exports.handler = async (event) => {
  const secretsManager = new SecretsManagerClient();
  
  // Generate new password

  // Update database user password

  // Update secret

};
```

```bash
  connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@localhost:5432/mydb" \
  allowed_roles="app-role" \
  username="vault" \
  password="vault-password"

vault write database/roles/app-role \
  db_name=postgresql \
  creation_statements="CREATE ROLE \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}'; \
    GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO \"{{name}}\";" \
  default_ttl="1h" \
  max_ttl="24h"
```

**Cost:** Free (open source) or $125+/month (enterprise)

---

### Option 3: Azure Key Vault (Best for Azure deployments)

**Advantages:**
- ✅ Native Azure integration
- ✅ Managed HSM option
- ✅ Azure AD authentication
- ✅ Soft-delete and purge protection
- ✅ Certificate management
- ✅ Key rotation

**Setup:**

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install @azure/keyvault-secrets @azure/identity

# Create Key Vault
az keyvault create \
  --name my-app-keyvault \
  --resource-group my-resource-group \
  --location eastus

# Set secrets
az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name my-app-keyvault \
  --name jwt-secret \
  --value "your-jwt-secret"

az keyvault secret set \
  --vault-name my-app-keyvault \
  --name database-url \
  --value "postgres://..."

# Grant access to managed identity
az keyvault set-policy \
  --name my-app-keyvault \
  --object-id <managed-identity-id> \
  --secret-permissions get list
```

**Cost:** ~$0.03/10,000 operations + HSM costs if needed

### Option 4: Google Cloud Secret Manager (Best for GCP)

```bash
# Install dependencies

# Create secrets
gcloud secrets create jwt-secret \
```

#!/bin/bash

# Secrets Security Audit Script
# Run this script to check for security issues with secrets management

set -e

echo "🔍 Running Secrets Security Audit..."
echo "======================================"
echo ""

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Track issues
CRITICAL_ISSUES=0
HIGH_ISSUES=0
MEDIUM_ISSUES=0

# Check 1: Look for .env files in repository
echo "1. Checking for .env files..."
ENV_FILES=$(find . -name ".env*" -not -name ".env.example" -not -path "./node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$ENV_FILES" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}❌ CRITICAL: Found .env files that should not be committed:${NC}"
    echo "$ENV_FILES"
    CRITICAL_ISSUES=$((CRITICAL_ISSUES + 1))
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ No .env files found${NC}"
fi
echo ""

# Check 2: Verify .gitignore exists and excludes .env files
echo "2. Checking .gitignore configuration..."
if [ ! -f .gitignore ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}❌ CRITICAL: .gitignore file missing${NC}"
    CRITICAL_ISSUES=$((CRITICAL_ISSUES + 1))
elif ! grep -q "^\.env" .gitignore; then
    echo -e "${RED}❌ CRITICAL: .gitignore doesn't exclude .env files${NC}"
    CRITICAL_ISSUES=$((CRITICAL_ISSUES + 1))
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ .gitignore properly configured${NC}"
fi
echo ""

# Check 3: Search for hardcoded secrets patterns
echo "3. Scanning for hardcoded secrets in code..."
SECRETS_FOUND=0

# Pattern matching for common secret patterns
PATTERNS=(
    "password\s*=\s*['\"][^'\"]{8,}"
    "api[_-]?key\s*=\s*['\"][^'\"]{20,}"
    "secret\s*=\s*['\"][^'\"]{20,}"
    "token\s*=\s*['\"][^'\"]{20,}"
    "AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"  # AWS Access Key
    "sk-live-[0-9a-zA-Z]{24,}"  # Stripe Live Key
    "sk-ant-[0-9a-zA-Z-]{20,}"  # Anthropic API Key
    "postgres://[^:]+:[^@]+@"  # Database URL with password
)

for pattern in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do
    MATCHES=$(grep -r -E "$pattern" --include="*.js" --include="*.ts" --exclude-dir=node_modules . 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ Found potential hardcoded secret:${NC}"
        echo "$MATCHES" | head -3
        SECRETS_FOUND=$((SECRETS_FOUND + 1))
    fi
done

if [ $SECRETS_FOUND -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ No obvious hardcoded secrets found${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${RED}Found $SECRETS_FOUND potential hardcoded secrets${NC}"
    HIGH_ISSUES=$((HIGH_ISSUES + SECRETS_FOUND))
fi
echo ""

# Check 4: Scan Git history for secrets
echo "4. Scanning Git history for leaked secrets..."
if [ -d .git ]; then
    HISTORY_SECRETS=$(git log -p | grep -i -E "password|secret|key|token" | wc -l)
    if [ $HISTORY_SECRETS -gt 10 ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  WARNING: Found $HISTORY_SECRETS potential secrets in Git history${NC}"
        echo "   Consider using: git filter-branch or BFG Repo-Cleaner"
        HIGH_ISSUES=$((HIGH_ISSUES + 1))
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Git history looks clean${NC}"
    fi
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  Not a Git repository${NC}"
fi
echo ""

# Check 5: Check for secrets manager implementation
echo "5. Checking for secrets manager implementation..."
if [ -f "config/secrets.js" ] || [ -f "config/vault-secrets.js" ] || [ -f "config/azure-secrets.js" ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Secrets manager configuration found${NC}"
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  WARNING: No secrets manager configuration found${NC}"
    echo "   Using environment variables directly is not recommended for production"
    MEDIUM_ISSUES=$((MEDIUM_ISSUES + 1))
fi
echo ""

# Check 6: Verify required security packages
echo "6. Checking for security packages..."
REQUIRED_PACKAGES=("helmet" "express-rate-limit" "express-validator")
MISSING_PACKAGES=0

if [ -f package.json ]; then
    for pkg in "${REQUIRED_PACKAGES[@]}"; do
        if ! grep -q "\"$pkg\"" package.json; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  Missing security package: $pkg${NC}"
            MISSING_PACKAGES=$((MISSING_PACKAGES + 1))
        fi
    done
    
    if [ $MISSING_PACKAGES -eq 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All recommended security packages present${NC}"
    else
        MEDIUM_ISSUES=$((MEDIUM_ISSUES + MISSING_PACKAGES))
    fi
else
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  package.json not found${NC}"
fi
echo ""

# Check 7: File permissions
echo "7. Checking file permissions..."
INSECURE_FILES=$(find . -name "*.env*" -perm -004 -not -path "./node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$INSECURE_FILES" ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  WARNING: .env files with world-readable permissions:${NC}"
    echo "$INSECURE_FILES"
    MEDIUM_ISSUES=$((MEDIUM_ISSUES + 1))
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ File permissions look good${NC}"
fi
echo ""

# Check 8: Docker secrets check
echo "8. Checking Docker configuration..."
if [ -f Dockerfile ]; then
    DOCKER_SECRETS=$(grep -E "ENV.*PASSWORD|ENV.*SECRET|ENV.*KEY" Dockerfile 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$DOCKER_SECRETS" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ CRITICAL: Secrets found in Dockerfile${NC}"
        echo "$DOCKER_SECRETS"
        CRITICAL_ISSUES=$((CRITICAL_ISSUES + 1))
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ No secrets in Dockerfile${NC}"
    fi
else
    echo -e "  No Dockerfile found (skipping)"
fi
echo ""

# Summary
echo "======================================"
echo "📊 AUDIT SUMMARY"
echo "======================================"
echo -e "Critical Issues: ${RED}$CRITICAL_ISSUES${NC}"
echo -e "High Issues: ${YELLOW}$HIGH_ISSUES${NC}"
echo -e "Medium Issues: ${YELLOW}$MEDIUM_ISSUES${NC}"
echo ""

if [ $CRITICAL_ISSUES -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}🚨 CRITICAL ISSUES FOUND - IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "Recommended actions:"
    echo "1. Remove .env files from repository"
    echo "2. Rotate all exposed credentials"
    echo "3. Add .env to .gitignore"
    echo "4. Clean Git history: git filter-branch or BFG Repo-Cleaner"
    exit 1
elif [ $HIGH_ISSUES -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  HIGH PRIORITY ISSUES - ADDRESS SOON${NC}"
    exit 1
elif [ $MEDIUM_ISSUES -gt 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  MEDIUM PRIORITY ISSUES - SHOULD FIX${NC}"
    exit 0
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✅ All checks passed!${NC}"
    exit 0
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Secret Rotation Script for AWS Secrets Manager
# This script demonstrates how to rotate secrets safely

set -e

SECRET_NAME=$1
REGION=${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}

if [ -z "$SECRET_NAME" ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <secret-name>"
    echo "Example: $0 app/jwt"
    exit 1
fi

echo "🔄 Starting secret rotation for: $SECRET_NAME"
echo "Region: $REGION"
echo ""

# Step 1: Generate new secret value
echo "1. Generating new secret value..."
NEW_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
echo "✓ New secret generated"
echo ""

# Step 2: Create a new version of the secret
echo "2. Creating new secret version in AWS Secrets Manager..."
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
    --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
    --secret-string "{\"secret\":\"$NEW_SECRET\"}" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --version-stages AWSPENDING

echo "✓ New secret version created with stage: AWSPENDING"
echo ""

# Step 3: Test the new secret
echo "3. Testing new secret..."
# Add your application-specific test here
# Example: Try to start a test instance with the new secret
echo "⚠️  Manual verification required:"
echo "   - Deploy to canary/test environment"
echo "   - Verify application functionality"
echo "   - Check authentication/connections work"
echo ""

read -p "Has testing passed? (yes/no): " TESTING_PASSED

if [ "$TESTING_PASSED" != "yes" ]; then
    echo "❌ Rotation aborted. Old secret remains active."
    echo "   Deleting AWSPENDING version..."
    
    # Remove the AWSPENDING stage
    CURRENT_VERSION=$(aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
        --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
        --region "$REGION" \
        --query 'VersionIdsToStages' \
        --output json | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value[] == "AWSPENDING") | .key')
    
    if [ -n "$CURRENT_VERSION" ]; then
        aws secretsmanager update-secret-version-stage \
            --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
            --remove-from-version-id "$CURRENT_VERSION" \
            --version-stage AWSPENDING \
            --region "$REGION"
    fi
    
    exit 1
fi

# Step 4: Promote the new secret to current
echo ""
echo "4. Promoting new secret to AWSCURRENT..."

# Get the version IDs
CURRENT_VERSION=$(aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
    --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --query 'VersionIdsToStages' \
    --output json | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value[] == "AWSCURRENT") | .key')

PENDING_VERSION=$(aws secretsmanager describe-secret \
    --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
    --region "$REGION" \
    --query 'VersionIdsToStages' \
    --output json | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value[] == "AWSPENDING") | .key')

# Move AWSCURRENT to AWSPREVIOUS and AWSPENDING to AWSCURRENT
aws secretsmanager update-secret-version-stage \
    --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
    --version-stage AWSCURRENT \
    --move-to-version-id "$PENDING_VERSION" \
    --remove-from-version-id "$CURRENT_VERSION" \
    --region "$REGION"

aws secretsmanager update-secret-version-stage \
    --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
    --version-stage AWSPREVIOUS \
    --move-to-version-id "$CURRENT_VERSION" \
    --region "$REGION"

echo "✓ Secret rotation complete!"
echo ""
echo "Version History:"
echo "  - AWSCURRENT: $PENDING_VERSION (new secret)"
echo "  - AWSPREVIOUS: $CURRENT_VERSION (old secret)"
echo ""

# Step 5: Wait for propagation
echo "5. Waiting for changes to propagate..."
sleep 30
echo "✓ Propagation complete"
echo ""

# Step 6: Verify production is using new secret
echo "6. Production verification..."
echo "⚠️  Please verify:"
echo "   - All application instances have restarted"
echo "   - All services are healthy"
echo "   - No authentication errors in logs"
echo ""

read -p "Is production stable? (yes/no): " PRODUCTION_STABLE

if [ "$PRODUCTION_STABLE" != "yes" ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Rolling back to previous secret..."
    
    aws secretsmanager update-secret-version-stage \
        --secret-id "$SECRET_NAME" \
        --version-stage AWSCURRENT \
        --move-to-version-id "$CURRENT_VERSION" \
        --remove-from-version-id "$PENDING_VERSION" \
        --region "$REGION"
    
    echo "✓ Rollback complete. Old secret is active again."
    exit 1
fi

# Step 7: Schedule old secret for deletion
echo ""
echo "7. Old secret will be kept as AWSPREVIOUS for emergency rollback"
echo "   To permanently delete old versions:"
echo "   aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id $SECRET_NAME --version-id $CURRENT_VERSION --region $REGION"
echo ""

# Log rotation
echo "📝 Logging rotation event..."
cat >> /var/log/secret-rotations.log <<EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")",
  "secret_name": "$SECRET_NAME",
  "old_version": "$CURRENT_VERSION",
  "new_version": "$PENDING_VERSION",
  "status": "success",
  "operator": "$(whoami)"
}
EOF

echo "✅ Secret rotation completed successfully!"
echo ""
echo "Summary:"
echo "  - Secret: $SECRET_NAME"
echo "  - Old Version: $CURRENT_VERSION (available for rollback)"
echo "  - New Version: $PENDING_VERSION (now active)"
echo "  - Rotation Time: $(date)"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Monitor application logs for 24-48 hours"
echo "  2. If stable, schedule deletion of old version"
echo "  3. Update rotation schedule in documentation"

# Security Audit Report: app.js

**Date**: 2024  
**Application**: Express.js Application  
**Severity**: CRITICAL  

---

## Executive Summary

The current `app.js` implementation has **10 critical and high-severity vulnerabilities** that expose the application to multiple OWASP Top 10 threats. The application lacks fundamental security controls including authentication, input validation, rate limiting, and security headers.

**Risk Level**: 🔴 **CRITICAL - NOT PRODUCTION READY**

---

## Vulnerability Summary

| # | Vulnerability | Severity | OWASP | Status |
|---|--------------|----------|-------|---------|
| 1 | No Authentication | 🔴 CRITICAL | A01:2021 | Open |
| 2 | Missing Input Validation | 🔴 CRITICAL | A03:2021 | Open |
| 3 | No Security Headers | 🔴 HIGH | A05:2021 | Open |
| 4 | Missing Rate Limiting | 🔴 HIGH | A04:2021 | Open |
| 5 | No CORS Policy | 🟡 MEDIUM | A05:2021 | Open |
| 6 | Inadequate Error Handling | 🟡 MEDIUM | A05:2021 | Open |
| 7 | No Logging/Monitoring | 🟡 MEDIUM | A09:2021 | Open |
| 8 | PII Data Exposure | 🟡 MEDIUM | A02:2021 | Open |
| 9 | Hardcoded Configuration | 🟡 MEDIUM | A05:2021 | Open |
| 10 | Missing Body Parser Controls | 🟡 MEDIUM | A03:2021 | Open |

---

## Detailed Findings

### 🔴 CRITICAL: VUL-001 - No Authentication on Sensitive Endpoint

**Location**: Line 11-16 (`/users` endpoint)  
**OWASP**: A01:2021 - Broken Access Control  
**CWE**: CWE-306 - Missing Authentication for Critical Function

**Description**:
The `/users` endpoint exposes personally identifiable information (names and email addresses) without any authentication mechanism.

**Current Code**:
```javascript
app.get('/users', (req, res) => {
  res.json([
    { id: 1, name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Bob', email: 'bob@example.com' },
  ]);
});
```

**Attack Scenario**:
1. Attacker sends: `curl http://example.com/users`
2. Receives full user database with emails
3. Can use emails for phishing or account enumeration

**Impact**: 
- Unauthorized data access
- Privacy violation
- GDPR violation (if EU users)
- Potential for targeted phishing attacks

**Recommendation**: Implement JWT-based authentication (see app.secure.js lines 130-151)

**Remediation Effort**: 4 hours

---

### 🔴 CRITICAL: VUL-002 - Missing Input Validation Framework

**OWASP**: A03:2021 - Injection  
**CWE**: CWE-20 - Improper Input Validation

**Description**:
No input validation middleware is configured. Any future POST/PUT endpoints will be vulnerable to injection attacks.

**Potential Attack Code**:
```javascript
// If someone adds this endpoint later:
app.post('/users', (req, res) => {
  const query = `INSERT INTO users VALUES ('${req.body.name}')`;
  // SQL Injection vulnerability!
});
```

**Impact**:
- SQL Injection
- NoSQL Injection
- Command Injection
- XSS attacks

**Recommendation**: Install and configure express-validator (see app.secure.js lines 116-127)

**Remediation Effort**: 2 hours

---

### 🔴 HIGH: VUL-003 - Missing Security Headers

**OWASP**: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration  
**CWE**: CWE-16 - Configuration

**Description**:
No security headers are set, leaving the application vulnerable to:
- Clickjacking (no X-Frame-Options)
- MIME sniffing attacks (no X-Content-Type-Options)
- XSS attacks (no Content-Security-Policy)
- Insecure connections (no HSTS)

**Test Results**:
```bash
$ curl -I http://localhost:3000/health
# No security headers present
```

**Impact**:
- XSS attacks
- Clickjacking
- MIME-type confusion attacks
- Man-in-the-middle attacks

**Recommendation**: Implement Helmet middleware (see app.secure.js lines 52-69)

**Remediation Effort**: 1 hour

---

### 🔴 HIGH: VUL-004 - No Rate Limiting

**OWASP**: A04:2021 - Insecure Design  
**CWE**: CWE-770 - Allocation of Resources Without Limits

**Description**:
No rate limiting allows unlimited requests, enabling:
- Denial of Service (DoS) attacks
- Brute force attacks (if login exists)
- Resource exhaustion

**Attack Scenario**:
```bash
# Attacker can flood the server
$ while true; do curl http://example.com/users; done
```

**Impact**:
- Service disruption
- Increased infrastructure costs
- Brute force attacks
- Data scraping

**Recommendation**: Implement express-rate-limit (see app.secure.js lines 99-113)

**Remediation Effort**: 2 hours

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-005 - No CORS Configuration

**OWASP**: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration  
**CWE**: CWE-346 - Origin Validation Error

**Description**:
No CORS policy means any website can make requests to this API.

**Attack Scenario**:
```javascript
// Malicious website can do:
fetch('http://victim-api.com/users')
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(data => sendToAttacker(data));
```

**Impact**:
- Cross-site request forgery
- Unauthorized data access from malicious sites
- API abuse

**Recommendation**: Configure CORS with whitelist (see app.secure.js lines 71-84)

**Remediation Effort**: 1 hour

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-006 - Inadequate Error Handling

**OWASP**: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration  
**CWE**: CWE-209 - Information Exposure Through an Error Message

**Description**:
No error handling middleware. Unhandled errors will expose stack traces.

**Example**:
```javascript
// Any error will show full stack trace in production
TypeError: Cannot read property 'foo' of undefined
    at /app/app.js:23:15
    at Layer.handle [as handle_request] (/app/node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js:95:5)
    ...
```

**Impact**:
- Information disclosure
- Path disclosure
- Technology stack disclosure
- Aids in reconnaissance

**Recommendation**: Implement error handling middleware (see SECURITY_RECOMMENDATIONS.md)

**Remediation Effort**: 2 hours

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-007 - No Security Logging

**OWASP**: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures  
**CWE**: CWE-778 - Insufficient Logging

**Description**:
No logging mechanism to detect or investigate security incidents.

**Missing Logs**:
- Failed authentication attempts
- Rate limit violations
- Input validation failures
- Suspicious access patterns

**Impact**:
- Cannot detect attacks
- No audit trail
- Difficult incident response
- Compliance violations

**Recommendation**: Implement Winston + Morgan logging (see app.secure.js lines 31-48)

**Remediation Effort**: 3 hours

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-008 - PII Data Exposure

**OWASP**: A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures  
**CWE**: CWE-359 - Exposure of Private Information

**Description**:
Email addresses (PII) are exposed to all users without authorization checks.

**Compliance Impact**:
- GDPR Article 5 violation (data minimization)
- CCPA violation (unnecessary disclosure)
- Privacy Act violations

**Recommendation**: Implement data masking and role-based access (see app.secure.js lines 151-171)

**Remediation Effort**: 2 hours

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-009 - Hardcoded Configuration

**OWASP**: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration  
**CWE**: CWE-547 - Use of Hard-coded Security-Relevant Constants

**Description**:
Port number and potential future secrets are hardcoded.

**Current Code**:
```javascript
app.listen(3000, () => {
  console.log('Server running on port 3000');
});
```

**Impact**:
- Difficult to change configuration
- Secrets may be committed to version control
- Cannot use different configs for environments

**Recommendation**: Use environment variables with dotenv (see .env.example)

**Remediation Effort**: 1 hour

---

### 🟡 MEDIUM: VUL-010 - Missing Body Parser Controls

**OWASP**: A03:2021 - Injection  
**CWE**: CWE-400 - Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

**Description**:
No body parser configured, and future additions won't have size limits.

**Attack Scenario**:
```bash
# Attacker sends huge payload
curl -X POST http://example.com/users \
  -d @huge-file.json
```

**Impact**:
- Memory exhaustion
- Denial of service
- Payload-based attacks

**Recommendation**: Configure body parser with limits (see app.secure.js lines 86-88)

**Remediation Effort**: 0.5 hours

## Automated Rotation Script

```javascript
// rotate-and-log.js
const secretsManager = require('./secrets-manager');
const crypto = require('crypto');
const fs = require('fs');

async function rotateSecret(secretName) {
  const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();
  
  console.log(`[${timestamp}] Starting rotation for ${secretName}`);
  
  try {
    // Get current version ID (metadata only)
    const currentVersion = await secretsManager.getCurrentVersion(secretName);
    
    // Generate new secret
    const newSecret = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
    
    // Update in secrets manager
    const newVersion = await secretsManager.updateSecret(secretName, {
      value: newSecret
    });
    
    // Log metadata only (NO SECRET VALUES)
    const logEntry = {
      timestamp,
      secretName,
      previousVersionId: currentVersion.versionId,
      newVersionId: newVersion.versionId,
      rotatedBy: process.env.USER || 'automated-system',
      status: 'SUCCESS'
    };
    
    // Append to rotation log (metadata only)
    fs.appendFileSync(
      'rotation-log.json',
      JSON.stringify(logEntry, null, 2) + ',\n'
    );
    
    console.log(`[${timestamp}] Rotation completed successfully`);
    console.log('Previous version:', currentVersion.versionId);
    console.log('New version:', newVersion.versionId);
    
    return logEntry;
    
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[${timestamp}] Rotation failed:`, error.message);
    
    const logEntry = {
      timestamp,
      secretName,
      status: 'FAILED',
      error: error.message
    };
    
    fs.appendFileSync(
      'rotation-log.json',
      JSON.stringify(logEntry, null, 2) + ',\n'
    );
    
    throw error;
  }
}

// Example usage
rotateSecret('myapp/production/JWT_SECRET')
  .then(() => console.log('Rotation complete'))
  .catch(err => {
    console.error('Rotation failed:', err);
    process.exit(1);
  });
```

- ✅ Compliance requirements for audit trails

- ❌ Creating additional attack surface

# Security Testing Guide

This guide provides practical tests to verify security controls are working correctly.

## Prerequisites

```bash
# Install testing dependencies
npm install --save-dev jest supertest

# Install security scanning tools
npm install -g snyk
npm install -g eslint eslint-plugin-security
```

---

## 1. Manual Security Tests

### Authentication Tests

#### Test 1: Access Protected Endpoint Without Token
```bash
# Should return 401 Unauthorized
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Unauthorized","message":"Access token is required"}
```

#### Test 2: Access with Invalid Token
```bash
# Should return 403 Forbidden
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer invalid_token_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Forbidden","message":"Invalid or expired token"}
```

#### Test 3: Access with Valid Token
```bash
# Should return 200 OK with user data
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_VALID_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

---

### Input Validation Tests

#### Test 4: SQL Injection Attempt
```bash
# Should be blocked by validation
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/api/users/1' OR '1'='1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Bad Request","message":"Invalid id format"}
```

#### Test 5: XSS Attempt in User Input
```bash
# Should be sanitized
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "<script>alert(\"XSS\")</script>",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "password": "SecureP@ss123"
  }'

# Name should be escaped: <script>alert("XSS")</script>
```

#### Test 6: Invalid Email Format
```bash
# Should be rejected
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Test User",
    "email": "not-an-email",
    "password": "SecureP@ss123"
  }'

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Bad Request","message":"Invalid email format"}
```

#### Test 7: Weak Password
```bash
# Should be rejected if password validation is enabled
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Test User",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "password": "weak"
  }'

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Validation Error","message":"..."}
```

---

### Rate Limiting Tests

#### Test 8: Rate Limit Enforcement
```bash
# Send multiple requests rapidly
for i in {1..110}; do
  curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
  echo "Request $i"
done

# After ~100 requests, should return:
# {"error":"Too Many Requests","message":"Too many requests, please try again later."}
```

---

### Authorization Tests

#### Test 9: Access Another User's Data
```bash
# User ID 1 trying to access User ID 2's data
# Should return 403 Forbidden (unless admin)
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users/2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer USER_1_TOKEN"

# Expected Response:
# {"error":"Forbidden","message":"You can only access your own resources"}
```

#### Test 10: Admin Access
```bash
# Admin should be able to access any user's data
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN"

# Expected Response: 200 OK with user data
```

---

### Security Headers Tests

#### Test 11: Check Security Headers
```bash
curl -I http://localhost:3000/health

# Should see headers like:
# X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
# X-Frame-Options: DENY
# X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
# Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
# Content-Security-Policy: ...
```

---

### CORS Tests

#### Test 12: CORS Policy
```bash
# Request from unauthorized origin
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/api/users \
  -H "Origin: https://evil.com" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -v 2>&1 | grep -i "access-control"

# Should NOT see Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.com
```

## 2. Automated Security Tests (Jest + Supertest)

Create `tests/security.test.js`:

```javascript
const request = require('supertest');
const app = require('../app.secure');

describe('Security Tests', () => {
  
  describe('Authentication', () => {
    test('Should reject requests without token', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/api/users')
        .expect(401);
      
      expect(res.body).toHaveProperty('error', 'Unauthorized');
    });
    
    test('Should reject requests with invalid token', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/api/users')
        .set('Authorization', 'Bearer invalid_token')
        .expect(403);
      
      expect(res.body).toHaveProperty('error', 'Forbidden');
    });
  });
  
  describe('Input Validation', () => {
    test('Should reject SQL injection attempts', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/api/users/1\' OR \'1\'=\'1')
        .set('Authorization', 'Bearer valid_token')
        .expect(400);
      
      expect(res.body).toHaveProperty('error', 'Bad Request');
    });
    
    test('Should reject invalid email format', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .post('/api/users')
        .send({
          name: 'Test',
          email: 'not-an-email',
          password: 'SecureP@ss123'
        })
        .expect(400);
      
      expect(res.body.message).toContain('email');
    });
    
    test('Should sanitize XSS attempts', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .post('/api/users')
        .send({
          name: '<script>alert("xss")</script>',
          email: 'test@example.com',
          password: 'SecureP@ss123'
        })
        .expect(201);
      
      // Name should be escaped
      expect(res.body.data.name).not.toContain('<script>');
    });
  });
  
  describe('Security Headers', () => {
    test('Should include security headers', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/health')
        .expect(200);
      
      expect(res.headers).toHaveProperty('x-content-type-options', 'nosniff');
      expect(res.headers).toHaveProperty('x-frame-options', 'DENY');
      expect(res.headers).not.toHaveProperty('x-powered-by');
    });
  });
  
  describe('Rate Limiting', () => {
    test('Should enforce rate limits', async () => {
      const requests = [];
      
      // Send 101 requests
      for (let i = 0; i < 101; i++) {
        requests.push(
          request(app)
            .get('/api/users')
            .set('Authorization', 'Bearer valid_token')
        );
      }
      
      const responses = await Promise.all(requests);
      const rateLimited = responses.filter(r => r.status === 429);
      
      expect(rateLimited.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }, 30000); // 30 second timeout
  });
  
  describe('Authorization', () => {
    test('Should prevent unauthorized access to other user data', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/api/users/999')
        .set('Authorization', 'Bearer user_1_token')
        .expect(403);
      
      expect(res.body).toHaveProperty('error', 'Forbidden');
    });
  });
  
  describe('Error Handling', () => {
    test('Should not leak sensitive error details', async () => {
      const res = await request(app)
        .get('/api/users/cause-error')
        .set('Authorization', 'Bearer valid_token');
      
      // Should not expose stack traces in production
      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {
        expect(res.body).not.toHaveProperty('stack');
      }
    });
  });
});
```

set -e

ENV="${ENVIRONMENT:-prod}"

echo "=========================================="

echo "Environment: $ENV"
echo ""

# Function to create or update a secret
create_secret() {
  local SECRET_NAME="$1"
  local SECRET_VALUE="$2"
  local DESCRIPTION="$3"

  echo "Creating/updating secret: ${ENV}/${SECRET_NAME}"

  # Try to create the secret
  aws secretsmanager create-secret \
    --name "${ENV}/${SECRET_NAME}" \
    --description "$DESCRIPTION" \
    --secret-string "$SECRET_VALUE" \
    --region "$REGION" 2>/dev/null || \
  # If it exists, update it
  aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
    --secret-id "${ENV}/${SECRET_NAME}" \
    --secret-string "$SECRET_VALUE" \
    --region "$REGION"

  echo "✓ ${ENV}/${SECRET_NAME} created/updated"
  echo ""
}

}

# Secrets Management Guide

## 🔐 Overview

This application uses a comprehensive secrets management system that supports multiple cloud providers and development environments.

## 🚨 Critical Security Rules

### ❌ NEVER DO THIS:
- Commit `.env` files to version control
- Store secrets in code or configuration files
- Log secret values (even in development)
- Share secrets via email, Slack, or other insecure channels
- Use production secrets in development environments
- Store secrets in CI/CD environment variables (use secrets manager instead)

### ✅ ALWAYS DO THIS:
- Use a secrets manager in production (AWS, GCP, Azure, Vault)
- Rotate secrets regularly (at least every 90 days)
- Use different secrets for each environment
- Grant least-privilege access to secrets
- Audit secret access regularly
- Use service accounts instead of user credentials

---

## 🏗️ Architecture

### Secrets Manager (`secrets-manager.js`)
- Multi-provider support (AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, Environment)
- Automatic caching with TTL
- Secret rotation support
- Validation and error handling

### Configuration (`config.js`)
- Centralized configuration management
- Environment-specific secret loading
- Validation of required secrets
- Hot-reload support for secret rotation

---

## 🚀 Setup Instructions

### Development (Using .env files)

1. **Copy example environment file:**
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

2. **Fill in development secrets:**
   ```bash
   # Edit .env with your development secrets
   nano .env
   ```

3. **Set secrets provider:**
   ```bash
   SECRETS_PROVIDER=env
   ```

4. **Start application:**
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

### Production (Using AWS Secrets Manager)

1. **Install AWS CLI and configure credentials:**
   ```bash
   aws configure
   ```

2. **Run setup script:**
   ```bash
   ./setup-aws-secrets.sh
   ```

3. **Grant IAM permissions to your application:**
   ```json
   {
     "Version": "2012-10-17",
     "Statement": [
       {
         "Effect": "Allow",
         "Action": [
           "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue",
           "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret"
         ],
         "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:region:account:secret:prod/*"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

4. **Set environment variables:**
   ```bash
   export SECRETS_PROVIDER=aws
   export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
   export NODE_ENV=production
   ```

5. **Start application:**
   ```bash
   npm start
   ```

---

## 🌩️ Cloud Provider Configuration

### AWS Secrets Manager

**Environment Variables:**
```bash
SECRETS_PROVIDER=aws
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
```

**IAM Role Required:**
- `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`
- `secretsmanager:DescribeSecret`

**Secret Naming Convention:**
- Format: `{environment}/{secret_name}`
- Example: `prod/JWT_SECRET`

### GCP Secret Manager

**Environment Variables:**
```bash
SECRETS_PROVIDER=gcp
GCP_PROJECT_ID=your-project-id
```

**Service Account Permissions:**
- `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`

**Authentication:**
```bash
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/service-account-key.json"
```

### Azure Key Vault

**Environment Variables:**
```bash
SECRETS_PROVIDER=azure
AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL=https://your-vault.vault.azure.net/
```

**Authentication:**
- Uses DefaultAzureCredential (managed identity or Azure CLI)

**Required Permissions:**
- `Key Vault Secrets User`

### HashiCorp Vault

**Environment Variables:**
```bash
SECRETS_PROVIDER=vault
VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com:8200
VAULT_TOKEN=your-vault-token
VAULT_SECRET_PATH=secret/data
```

---

## 🔄 Secret Rotation

### Automatic Rotation (AWS)

1. **Create rotation Lambda function:**
   ```bash
   aws secretsmanager rotate-secret \
     --secret-id prod/JWT_SECRET \
     --rotation-lambda-arn arn:aws:lambda:region:account:function:rotation-function \
     --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30
   ```

### Manual Rotation

1. **Update secret in secrets manager**
2. **Trigger reload via API:**
   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://api.example.com/admin/rotate-secrets \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
   ```

---

## 🔍 Monitoring & Auditing

### CloudWatch Alarms (AWS)

```bash
# Alert on secret access failures
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name secret-access-failures \
  --metric-name SecretAccessFailures \
  --threshold 5 \
  --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold
```

### Access Logging

All secret access is logged with:
- Timestamp
- Secret name (not value)
- Requesting service
- Success/failure status

### Audit Trail

Query CloudTrail for secret access:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events \
  --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceType,AttributeValue=AWS::SecretsManager::Secret \
  --max-results 50
```

## 🚨 Incident Response

### If a Secret is Compromised:

1. **Immediately rotate the secret:**
   ```bash
   ./setup-aws-secrets.sh
   ```

2. **Revoke compromised credentials:**
   ```bash
   aws secretsmanager delete-secret \
     --secret-id prod/COMPROMISED_SECRET \
   ```

#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit - Prevent committing secrets

set -e

echo "Running pre-commit security checks..."

# Colors
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Check for secrets in staged files
FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS=(
  "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
  "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
  "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
  "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"
  "sk-live-"
  "sk-ant-"
  "postgres://.*:.*@"
  "mysql://.*:.*@"
  "mongodb://.*:.*@"
  "api[_-]?key.*=.*['\"][a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}['\"]"
  "secret.*=.*['\"][a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}['\"]"
  "password.*=.*['\"][^'\"]{8,}['\"]"
  "AKIA-I[A-Z0-9]{16}"
  "private[_-]key"
  "-----BEGIN (RSA|DSA|EC|OPENSSH) PRIVATE KEY-----"
)

# Files to check
FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM)

SECRETS_FOUND=0

for FILE in $FILES; do
  # Skip binary files
  if file "$FILE" | grep -q "text"; then
    for PATTERN in "${FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
      if grep -iEq "$PATTERN" "$FILE"; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ Potential secret found in $FILE${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}   Pattern: $PATTERN${NC}"
        grep -inE "$PATTERN" "$FILE" | head -3
        SECRETS_FOUND=1
      fi
    done
  fi
done

# Check if .env files are being committed
ENV_FILES=$(echo "$FILES" | grep -E '^\.env$|^\.env\..*$' | grep -v '.env.example' | grep -v '.env.production' || true)

if [ -n "$ENV_FILES" ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}❌ Attempting to commit .env file(s):${NC}"
  echo "$ENV_FILES"
  echo -e "${YELLOW}   .env files should never be committed!${NC}"
  SECRETS_FOUND=1
fi

# Check for large files (potential credential dumps)
LARGE_FILES=$(echo "$FILES" | xargs -I {} du -k {} 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 > 1024 {print $2}' || true)

if [ -n "$LARGE_FILES" ]; then
  echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  Warning: Large files detected (>1MB):${NC}"
  echo "$LARGE_FILES"
  echo -e "${YELLOW}   Ensure these don't contain secrets or sensitive data${NC}"
fi

if [ $SECRETS_FOUND -eq 1 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo -e "${RED}========================================${NC}"
  echo -e "${RED}COMMIT BLOCKED: Potential secrets detected${NC}"
  echo -e "${RED}========================================${NC}"
  echo ""
  echo "To fix:"
  echo "1. Remove secrets from the files"
  echo "2. Add secrets to .gitignore"
  echo "3. Use secrets manager instead"
  echo ""
  echo "If this is a false positive, you can:"
  echo "- Review the patterns and update .git/hooks/pre-commit"
  echo "- Use: git commit --no-verify (NOT RECOMMENDED)"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}✓ No secrets detected${NC}"

# Run additional checks
echo "Running linter..."
npm run lint --silent || {
  echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  Linting failed. Fix issues before committing.${NC}"
  exit 1
}

echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All pre-commit checks passed${NC}"
exit 0

# Security Checklist for Secrets Management

## 🔐 Deployment Checklist

### Before Production Deployment

- [ ] All secrets removed from code and configuration files
- [ ] `.gitignore` configured to exclude `.env` files
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks installed to prevent secret commits
- [ ] Secrets migrated to secrets manager (AWS/GCP/Azure/Vault)
- [ ] IAM/RBAC permissions configured with least privilege
- [ ] Service accounts created (not using personal credentials)
- [ ] All production secrets are unique (not shared with dev/staging)
- [ ] Secrets are encrypted at rest
- [ ] Secrets are transmitted over TLS only
- [ ] Database credentials use minimal required permissions
- [ ] API keys have rate limiting and IP restrictions enabled
- [ ] Secret rotation schedule established (every 90 days)
- [ ] Access logging enabled for secrets manager
- [ ] Monitoring alerts configured for:
  - [ ] Failed secret access attempts
  - [ ] Secret modification events
  - [ ] Unusual access patterns
- [ ] Incident response plan documented
- [ ] Team trained on secrets management procedures

### Environment Configuration

- [ ] `SECRETS_PROVIDER` set to appropriate cloud provider
- [ ] `NODE_ENV` set to `production`
- [ ] Cloud provider credentials configured (IAM role, managed identity, etc.)
- [ ] No secrets in environment variables
- [ ] No secrets in container images
- [ ] No secrets in CI/CD configuration
- [ ] Secrets not logged or printed

### Secret Inventory

- [ ] JWT signing key (`JWT_SECRET`)
- [ ] Database connection string (`DATABASE_URL`)
- [ ] Cloud provider credentials (if needed)
- [ ] Third-party API keys (Stripe, Anthropic, etc.)
- [ ] Logging service tokens
- [ ] Encryption keys
- [ ] TLS certificates and private keys

### Code Review

- [ ] No hardcoded credentials
- [ ] No commented-out secrets
- [ ] Secrets not in error messages
- [ ] Secrets not in logs
- [ ] Input validation for all secret-related operations
- [ ] Error handling doesn't leak secret information
- [ ] Secrets never sent to client
- [ ] No secrets in URLs or query parameters
- [ ] No secrets in client-side code

### Testing

- [ ] Secrets mocked in unit tests
- [ ] Test secrets different from production
- [ ] Integration tests use dedicated test environment
- [ ] Secrets cleanup after test runs
- [ ] No production secrets in test data

### Monitoring

- [ ] CloudWatch/Cloud Logging configured
- [ ] Alert on secret access failures
- [ ] Alert on secret modifications
- [ ] Alert on secret deletion
- [ ] Audit trail retention configured (90+ days)
- [ ] Regular review of access logs

### Documentation

- [ ] Secrets management guide created
- [ ] Team onboarding includes secrets training
- [ ] Incident response procedures documented
- [ ] Secret rotation procedures documented
- [ ] Recovery procedures documented

### Compliance

- [ ] GDPR compliance (if applicable)
- [ ] PCI DSS compliance (if handling payments)
- [ ] SOC 2 requirements met (if applicable)
- [ ] Regular security audits scheduled
- [ ] Penetration testing includes secrets management
